title: A crawler factory shows how to scale bounded coding-agent work
friendlyTitle: Small agent jobs helped build a large concert database
summary: ClassicalBot describes using Codex agents to build website-specific concert crawlers from a URL queue. Deterministic validation, one controlled retry, GitHub pull requests, and automated checks helped the project expand to more than 70,000 future concerts from over 4,000 sources.
friendlySummary: ClassicalBot sends website addresses to coding agents, which build one concert crawler at a time. Automatic tests and GitHub checks decide whether each crawler is good enough to keep.
whyItMatters: The workflow is a practical blueprint for scaling many independent, bounded tasks: queue small jobs, validate outputs mechanically, limit retries, and route changes through version control. The same shape can apply to catalogues, prices, events, or other structured-data work.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Breaking work into small jobs with clear tests can make agent automation easier to control and reuse.
